correctness.rationale: For a strictly convex 2r-gon with genuine antipodally matched outward edge-normal fan, a noncritical illumination direction has exactly r consecutive edge normals with negative dot product and therefore illuminates exactly L=r−1 consecutive vertices. Critical directions strictly reduce the count. Incidence counting forces N≥ceil(2rk/L) for k-fold multicover and mass≥2r/L fractional. The balanced discrete start positions floor((2r)j/N) cyclically cover each length-L window either floor(NL/(2r)) or ceil, attaining integer bound; assigning 1/L to each of 2r generic direction cells attains fractional bound. At optimum all mass is off critical rays and every vertex constraint tight, giving cyclic equations sum_{h=0}^{L−1}w_{i−h}=1. Their differences force w_i=w_{i−L}; gcd(2r,r−1)=1 for r even, =2 for r odd, yielding unique uniform or alternating one-parameter solutions. The explicit rational hexagon has positive side lengths, closed edge chain and strictly positive turns but unequal opposite lengths and unequal consecutive angle dot products. Separately checked multiple concrete integer cover cases and rational identities; finite samples not asserted as universal proof.
